answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity accumulates a hashed profile of its interaction timing, message-size distribution, and counterparty overlap, stored as an onyx ledger entry per epoch. At epoch boundaries the agent recomputes the profile and requires divergence below a fixed threshold; a sudden jetty-style shift in any dimension flags the identity as fresh. Flagged identities must re-earn standing over three epochs with capped throughput, and any hollow account showing the same profile as a flagged one is merged and loses its queue priority.
